key_insight: Chow-form methods improve complexity bounds from PSPACE to the counting hierarchy (CH) for several algebraic-variety decomposition and membership problems.
engineering_relevance: These results sharpen theoretical limits for symbolic-computation tasks involving polynomial systems, component membership, and polynomial-map image closures.
method: Represent equidimensional components using Chow forms and geometric resolutions.
Construct polylogtime-uniform, constant-depth, exponential-size threshold circuits using multivariate-resultant circuits.
Derive CH decision procedures and an FP^CH algorithm for component degrees.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical complexity guarantees, including approximate polynomial satisfiability in CH, rather than numerical experiments or runtime benchmarks.
watch_item: Exponential circuit size means the improved complexity classification does not itself establish a practical implementation.
paper_title: Some algebraic and geometric computations in CH via Chow forms
